svg.title: Topological orders and parallelism
svg.desc: The example ADG, its two topological orders as arrays with parent indices, execution by dependencies (parallel) versus executing the array one entry at a time (serial), and the ready sets as the dispatcher sees them.

g.text: Edges (arrows) run parent -> child, always left to right. Each entry also stores p = its parents' indices,

g.text: all smaller than its own (ActionNode.parents). The order of unordered actions is arbitrary.

g.text: Durations as in the critical-path figure. The serial chart is what would happen if a consumer ignored parents and ran Schedule.nodes in index order.

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Topological orders do not remove parallelism

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: A topological order is a way to list a DAG, not a way to run it. The list keeps every edge (as parent indices); execution follows the edges, so unordered actions still run together.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
